post.caption:
Distant galaxies are all receding, and the further away they are the faster they go. We know because their light arrives redshifted, which is the Doppler effect applied to light. But they are not flying through space away from us. Space itself is expanding between them. Picture raisins in a rising loaf: every raisin sees every other one moving away, the further apart the faster, and no raisin is the centre. There is no centre in the loaf at all.
